answer: Every peat stack the crofter cuts is measured with the rod and entered in the fuel book, and the stack may be burned only when the measure matches. A pulse stack cut on another man's moss fails the measure: at the kernel of the peat the rods must match the crofter's own cut, and a strange stack burns damp and low. Faking the fuel means cutting peat for six weeks, stacking 2,000 turves and paying 3,900, while the reef figure in the fuel book is read at every hearth, so a stack whose measure was never entered is left to rot in the rain.
